in_hebrew.name: יעקב
in_hebrew.meaning: הוא יחליף, יעקב הוא שם עברי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם יעקב הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'הוא יחליף' או 'יחליף'. השם נגזר מהמילה העברית 'עקב', שפירושו 'עקב' או 'קשר'. השם יעקב מוזכר במקרא כבנו של יצחק ואביו של יוסף ויהודה. הוא היה אישיות חשובה בתולדות עם ישראל.

in_greek.name: Ιακώβος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιακώβος είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος יעקב (יעקב), που σημαίνει 'αντί να τον φτύνω' ή 'θα τον αντικαταστήσει'. Στο Ευαγγέλιο του Ματθαίου (Ματθαίος 1:2-16), το όνομα Ιακώβος αναφέρεται ως ο πατέρας του Ιωσήφ, του συζύγου της Μαρίας, της μητέρας του Ιησού.

in_latin.name: Iacobus
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Iacobus is derived from the Hebrew name יעקב (Ya'aqov), which means 'supplanter' or 'he who replaces'. In the Latin Vulgate, the name Iacobus is used to refer to James, the brother of Jesus and the leader of the church in Jerusalem.

in_english.name: Giacomo
in_english.meaning: supplanter, replacing, or he who supplants
in_english.long_meaning: The name Giacomo is the Italian form of the Hebrew name יעקב (Ya'aqov), which means 'supplanter', 'replacing', or 'he who supplants'. The name Giacomo is derived from the Greek name Ιακώβος (Iakōbos), which was used to refer to James, the brother of Jesus and the leader of the church in Jerusalem. Throughout history, the name Giacomo has been popularized in Italy and other Christian cultures, symbolizing spiritual significance, devotion, and faith.

data.cultural_impact: The name Giacomo has significant historical and artistic connections in Western civilization. Throughout history, several prominent figures have held this name, including numerous popes, artists (such as Giacomo Caravaggio), political figures (like Giacomo Casanova), and musicians (including opera singers and rock stars).
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Giacomo is identified with the apostle James, son of Zebedee, one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus Christ. James was also a brother of John and a fisherman by trade. According to the New Testament, James became the bishop of Jerusalem and, according to tradition, was martyred by being put to the sword. Consequently, the name comes with associations of faith, courage, and martyrdom.

historical_references.reference: Giacomo da Lentini, a Sicilian monk and scholar, is credited with translating the works of Aristotle into Latin during the 13th century. This translation, known as the 'Translatio Guadagniensis', greatly influenced the scholarly world and contributed to the revival of Aristotelian philosophy in Western Europe.
